cards.title: Where did agents say they were confused?

query_table_requests.title: Portable execution profiles and conformance fixtures
query_table_requests.gap: The new Go planner emits PostgreSQL casts/functions. Pharos runs SQLite and its own map executor; v2 is not available by changing frontend dependencies.
query_table_requests.proposal: Provide a dialect-neutral validated execution plan or a documented adapter seam plus portable semantic fixtures. Add a SQLite profile where appropriate, or let Pharos implement the same negotiated v2 contract without pretending every function is portable.
examples: All new all-matching formulas and distributions in Pharos
query_table_requests.performance: Retain SQLite indexes, FTS and cube routing. Hosts own actual execution, deadlines and prepared views; conformance checks cover nulls, errors, lazy branches and numeric precision.
query_table_requests.current_status: All ten schemas execute through the negotiated qt-sqlite-v1 profile, with canonical revisions, typed rows and integration/conformance coverage.

query_table_requests.title: An indexed search predicate seam
query_table_requests.gap: The host indexed message/Library search relation participates in V2/V3 counts and groups with explicit bounded-search coverage. A reusable upstream search seam remains a request.
query_table_requests.proposal: Let a host advertise a persisted, typed indexed-search predicate/source that participates in the same counts, groups and cache identity as ordinary filters. Define matched-row versus parent-membership semantics and bounded-search coverage; Pharos supplies FTS and excerpt hydration.
examples: Agent confusion in the last seven days
query_table_requests.performance: Apply role and message-time constraints to the match population. Do not replace indexed search with a regex scan of every transcript or filter workspace activity dates as if they were message dates.
query_table_requests.current_status: The host indexed message/Library search relation participates in V2/V3 counts and groups with explicit bounded-search coverage. A reusable upstream search seam remains a request.

query_table_requests.title: Grouped time series and heatmap presentation
query_table_requests.gap: Line charts are one chronological series; two-key output has a pivot/table route, but no explicit heatmap or shared stacked-series chart contract.
query_table_requests.proposal: Support time × category series with explicit missing/zero semantics, stacked or grouped marks, stable colors and an exact remainder; add a bounded two-key heatmap. Share full and compact renderers.
query_table_requests.performance: Bound time buckets and categories; preserve totals when folding an additive remainder. Do not smooth missing observations or sum rates across categories.
query_table_requests.current_status: Native line/bar series and pivots are available; Home retains calendar-aware Usage columns with shared colors. Native heatmaps and the full missing/zero/remainder series contract remain deferred.

query_table_requests.title: Bounded expansion of set-valued dimensions
query_table_requests.gap: Arrays support membership filtering but are not admitted server row expressions; grouping a host list is not grouping each member.
query_table_requests.proposal: Offer an explicit explode-members stage or a normalized host relation with declared parent identity. Define event-count versus membership-count measures and restrict simultaneous expansions to prevent accidental cross products.
examples: All files touched by a work
query_table_requests.performance: Index normalized members or materialize them during ingestion. Carry distinct parent IDs to avoid multiplying usage or costs across memberships.

query_table_requests.title: Editable bookmark metadata with stable IDs
query_table_requests.gap: SavedQuery carries name, timestamp and QueryState. StorageAdapter has saveNamed/delete, but no stable-ID update for name/description/order or discovery across dataset namespaces.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add optional stable-ID bookmark updates for title, description and user order, and a host-controlled way to enumerate relevant bookmarks across dataset namespaces. Keep queries as canonical storage and preserve existing adapters.
examples: Rename and describe a collected card
Keep one query identity across surfaces
query_table_requests.performance: This is storage/API work rather than metric computation. Metadata changes should not invalidate arithmetic or recreate saved IDs.
query_table_requests.current_status: Stable bookmark metadata, ordering and cross-dataset collection are host-owned. Optional coverMetricId selects a saved metric without changing the query or bookmark ID.

query_table_requests.title: Registered relationships with explicit cardinality
query_table_requests.gap: The host can already supply a joined SourceSQL, but users cannot compose registered dataset relationships.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider approved relation joins or semi-joins with declared grain and cardinality, not arbitrary SQL. Provide fanout-aware measures and source lineage.
query_table_requests.performance: Prejoin recurring relationships in Pharos first; index join keys and prevent multiplication of already-aggregated facts.

query_table_requests.title: Ordered partition functions
query_table_requests.gap: Formula context rejects windows and source order is not exposed as an analytical operation.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider LAG/LEAD, first/last-by-order, running counts and elapsed differences over a declared partition and stable event ordering.
query_table_requests.performance: Use partition/order indexes and bound the queried streams. Filter-after-window semantics may require earlier events outside a visible time window.

query_table_requests.title: Sessionization and event episode or funnel recipes
query_table_requests.gap: Recovery and verification episodes do not exist as generic metric inputs.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider deterministic, bounded sessionization and ordered-pattern extraction over typed events. Keep definitions explicit and let hosts supply materialized episode rows.
query_table_requests.performance: Repeated homepage requests should query episode facts updated on ingestion rather than recompute every transcript sequence. Episode-boundary definitions are often domain-specific.

query_table_requests.title: Interval union overlap and concurrency
query_table_requests.gap: SUM(duration) cannot compute wall time for parallel activity; no interval transform is exposed.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider typed interval-union length, overlap episodes and time-bucket occupancy as optional reducers or prepared host facts.
query_table_requests.performance: Sweep ordered interval endpoints rather than join every interval pair. Report open/missing endpoints and never substitute summed durations for elapsed time.

query_table_requests.title: Co-occurrence and association over prepared sets
query_table_requests.gap: File pairs and workflow motifs require pair/sequence creation and normalized marginal counts.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider bounded association reducers over prepared membership or edge datasets: support count, joint frequency and explicit marginals for lift. Keep pair generation and semantic labels in the host initially.
query_table_requests.performance: Pair expansion can be quadratic; cap set size, use incremental sparse counts and minimum support before ranking.

query_table_requests.title: Named scenario parameters and aligned variants
query_table_requests.gap: Literal arithmetic can already calculate a scenario once rates and inputs are fields, but no reusable parameter bundle or named variant output exists.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider typed saved parameters with units and several labeled variants over the same prepared population. Hosts supply rates and billing data.
query_table_requests.performance: Reuse workload projections across scenarios. Keep parameters out of display labels and external lookups out of expression execution.

query_table_requests.title: An optional result renderer registration seam
query_table_requests.gap: Current chart families do not render transcript excerpts, event paths, parallel lanes or trees.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider host-rendered result kinds with typed validated payloads, inspect callbacks, theme access and compact/full variants. Avoid building every domain-specific cover into the core library.
query_table_requests.performance: Bound nodes/edges/excerpts, preserve query identity and defer hydration. Keep nonserializable callbacks out of saved-query state.

query_table_requests.title: A batch scheduler for heterogeneous previews
query_table_requests.gap: A v2 metric batch shares one WHERE, while a carousel pool spans filters, windows and datasets.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider a reusable headless runner for several query plans with concurrency caps, cancellation, partial completion, memoization and visible-first priorities; the host may implement this without changing QueryState.
examples: Eligibility checks for a large suggestion pool
query_table_requests.performance: Group compatible candidates to share work, cache on explicit revisions/window anchors and fetch only a selected preview subset. Backend scan fusion is distinct from HTTP request batching.
query_table_requests.current_status: The headless preview runner batches compatible populations, caps metric batches at 20 and executions at three, publishes partial completion, isolates rejected formulas and supports cancellation and one-minute result reuse.

query_table_requests.title: Semantic interpretation inside metric expressions
query_table_requests.gap: Confusion loops, decisions, examples and scope changes require meaning extraction.
query_table_requests.proposal: Keep semantic extraction, embedding similarity and evidence-backed labels in Pharos. Query Table should consume their versioned annotations and indexed similarity result rows.
query_table_requests.performance: Do expensive extraction incrementally outside interactive queries; expose provenance and uncertain classifications.

query_table_requests.title: Automatic causal or quality judgments
query_table_requests.gap: Recorded outcomes and correlations cannot establish model superiority, productivity or cause.
query_table_requests.proposal: Offer explicit cohorts, denominators and underlying evidence. Keep domain scoring and recommendation ranking outside generic arithmetic; avoid a universal opaque success score.
query_table_requests.performance: Matched populations and statistical uncertainty are host/domain work; charting cannot solve confounding.

query_table_requests.title: Arbitrary SQL or recursive graph analytics in saved metrics
query_table_requests.gap: These would widen a deliberately allowlisted expression API into a general database language.
query_table_requests.proposal: Prefer registered sources, narrow relational stages and host-produced lineage closures or episode facts. Do not add raw user SQL, arbitrary recursive queries or unrestricted transcript regex as a homepage shortcut.
query_table_requests.performance: Unbounded graph/pair/text scans are poor interactive workloads and require host access and resource boundaries.

query_table_requests.title: Provider pricing billing or carbon models owned by Query Table
query_table_requests.gap: These require domain rate tables, assumptions and sometimes external/user data.
query_table_requests.proposal: Keep price books, billing inputs and energy models in Pharos. Query Table handles typed arithmetic, variants and visualization over prepared fields.
query_table_requests.performance: Version inputs and materialize compatible pricing components. Do not fetch providers as metric side effects.

query_table_requests.title: Automatically create database indexes or materializations for every saved formula
query_table_requests.gap: Expression execution does not imply a good database index, and definitions can change.
query_table_requests.proposal: Let the host measure plans and opt into projections, generated values, sketches or expression indexes. A core plan/explain hook is reasonable; automatic schema writes are not the default.
query_table_requests.performance: Account for ingestion/write cost, data volume and definition revisions; avoid proliferating expensive indexes for speculative cards.

capacity_audit.scope: All existing schema fields, SQL bindings, aggregate capabilities and retained data adapters reviewed. Narrow observed variants keep the original intended concept and its remaining evidence requirements.

human_word_review.description: Concise metric names, explicit-window human-writing descriptions, destination-specific CTAs, labelled trend extrema, fixed conversation size bands, and a concrete-feedback percentage trend.
human_word_review.denominators: Example/context percentages use assessed human contributions, including context-only messages. Workspace comparisons use contributions in each mapped repository/directory; no attribution to code changes is inferred.
